message.content: The kernel is a polynomial-approximation exp2. The two highest-risk, directly testable hypotheses: polynomial approximation error vs the 1e-6 relative tolerance, and combined FP32 rounding. Both are in-scope since the contract demands the tolerance for every legal BF16 value in [-10,10].

function.arguments: {"rationale": "A degree-6 polynomial with only 6 significant digits in its coefficients approximating 2^f on [-0.5,0.5] typically has minimax relative error near 1e-7, but coefficient rounding to 6 decimals can add up to ~1e-6 error itself, so worst-case points may exceed the 1e-6 relative-only tolerance.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - 2**x[i]) <= 1e-6 * 2**x[i], absolute tolerance zero, for EVERY finite BF16 value in [-10,10], one verdict for the whole domain."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract requires the 1e-6 relative tolerance for every legal input over the whole domain; a polynomial-accuracy failure at any BF16-representable x in [-10,10] directly violates the stated per-element bound.", "statement": "The degree-6 Horner polynomial for 2^fraction on [-0.5,0.5] has worst-case relative error that may exceed 1e-6 for some BF16-representable x in [-10,10], so run(x) violates the contract tolerance at those points."}
function.name: record_claim

function.arguments: {"rationale": "With enable_fp_fusion=False, each of ~6 multiply and 5 add operations in Horner form introduces up to 0.5 ulp FP32 relative error (~6e-8 each), summing to a few times 1e-7 on top of polynomial error, which could push total relative error past the 1e-6 bound even where the polynomial alone is within it.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Per-element bound abs(actual - 2**x) <= 1e-6 * 2**x with zero absolute tolerance applies to the entire legal domain; approximations are permitted only if they satisfy this fixed relative tolerance throughout."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract admits approximations only if the fixed 1e-6 relative tolerance holds throughout the entire legal domain, so accumulated FP32 rounding crossing 1e-6 at any legal input is a direct violation.", "statement": "Accumulated FP32 rounding across the six Horner multiply-add steps plus the final scale*polynomial multiply may push the combined relative error above 1e-6 for worst-case fractions even if the polynomial approximation error alone stays under the tolerance."}
function.name: record_claim

message.reasoning_content: Record claims: polynomial accuracy, combined FP32 rounding, maybe coefficient fit (this polynomial looks like a known degree-6 minimax for 2^f on [-0.5,0.5] with error ~1e-6... actually error near 1e-7). Record 2 claims in_scope.
